batchName: Late Republic: Marius and the Northern Invaders (121-100 BCE) - Easy Batch 1
chapterName: Late Republic: Marius and the Northern Invaders (121-100 BCE)

questions.question: Why, in part, did Rome keep re-electing Marius as consul during the northern threat?
options: To reward him for capturing Carthage
To avoid another clash between rival commanders
Because the Senate had been dissolved
Because no other candidates were legally eligible
questions.explanation: Romans wanted to avoid a repeat of Arausio, where feuding commanders had doomed the army. Marius's rebuilt army was drilled hard near Aquae Sextiae.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome kept re-electing him, partly to avoid another clash between rival commanders like the one that had doomed Arausio.

questions.question: Numidia, the kingdom at the centre of the war against Jugurtha, lay roughly in which modern country?
questions.explanation: Numidia lay on the north African coast, roughly modern Algeria. It had been a loyal ally of Rome since the wars against Carthage.
questions.sourceQuote: Numidia was a kingdom on the north African coast, roughly modern Algeria, and a loyal ally of Rome since the wars against Carthage (*Carthago*).

questions.question: What happened to Saturninus and the other prisoners locked in the Senate house?
options: A mob stoned them with roof tiles
questions.explanation: A mob climbed onto the roof, tore off the tiles and stoned the prisoners to death. This may have happened with Marius's tacit approval.
questions.sourceQuote: He locked them in the Senate house to await trial, but a mob climbed onto the roof, tore off the tiles and stoned the prisoners to death, possibly with Marius's tacit approval.

questions.question: Which aristocrat, known for honesty and courage, did the Senate send in 109 BC to take over the war against Jugurtha?
questions.explanation: The Senate sent Metellus after years of disgrace in the war. He retrained a slack army and chose officers for ability rather than rank.
questions.sourceQuote: After years of disgrace, the Senate sent Metellus, an aristocrat with a reputation for honesty and courage, to take over the war against Jugurtha, the defiant king of Numidia in north Africa.

questions.question: In Roman politics, what did it mean to call Marius a "new man" (novus homo)?
options: He was the youngest man ever elected consul
He had only recently been granted citizenship
He was the first of his family to reach high office
He had been adopted into a patrician family
questions.explanation: A novus homo was the first of his family to reach high office. The old aristocracy never let Marius forget his status as an outsider.
questions.sourceQuote: In Rome, though, Marius was a "new man" (*novus homo*), the first of his family to reach high office, and the old aristocracy never let him forget it.

questions.question: How many consulships in a row did Marius hold from 104 to 100 BC?
questions.explanation: Marius held five consecutive consulships from 104 to 100 BC, on top of his first in 107 BC. This placed unprecedented power in one man's hands.
questions.sourceQuote: In the end Marius held five consulships in a row, from 104 to 100 BC, on top of his first in 107 BC.

questions.question: Arausio in 105 BC was Rome's worst defeat since which earlier disaster?
questions.explanation: Arausio was Rome's worst defeat since Hannibal's victory at Cannae over a century earlier. Panic swept the city amid talk of the "Cimbrian terror".
questions.sourceQuote: Arausio was Rome's worst defeat since Hannibal's victory at Cannae over a century earlier.

questions.question: Near which hill town south-east of Rome was Gaius Marius born, around 157 BC?
questions.explanation: Marius was born near Arpinum, a hill town south-east of Rome. His family was locally prominent and wealthy, probably from large landholdings.
questions.sourceQuote: Gaius Marius, the outsider who would be elected to Rome's highest office more often than any man before him, was born around 157 BC near Arpinum, a hill town south-east of Rome.

questions.question: How did Marius force Saturninus and his rebels on the Capitoline Hill to surrender in 100 BC?
options: He set fire to the temple
He marched a legion into the city
He cut off their water supply
questions.explanation: Marius rallied volunteers and veterans and cut off the water supply to the Capitoline Hill. He refused to bring an army near the city.
questions.sourceQuote: Instead he rallied volunteers and veterans, cut off the water supply to the Capitoline Hill where the rebels held out, and forced their surrender.

questions.question: Where and when did the idea of the "Marian reforms" of the Roman army originate?
questions.explanation: The idea began with German scholars in the 1840s. Most specialists now call it a construct of modern scholarship.
questions.sourceQuote: The idea began with German scholars in the 1840s.
